The worker has scaffolded a minimal-host Program.cs for .NET Core 8.0, wired configuration sources, and deferred service and middleware registration to the existing Startup class. However, the call builder.Services.ConfigureServices(builder.Configuration) assumes the existence of an extension method that isn’t provided, so neither Startup.ConfigureServices nor the DI setup will actually run. To compile and execute as intended, you must either: 1) invoke Startup.ConfigureServices explicitly (e.g. var startup = new Startup(builder.Configuration); startup.ConfigureServices(builder.Services);), or 2) supply a ConfigureServices extension method that delegates to Startup.ConfigureServices. Without that, the services pipeline is never registered and the app will fail at runtime or not recognize controllers.
remark: The code calls builder.Services.ConfigureServices(...) but no such extension method is defined. You need to wire Startup.ConfigureServices into the builder.Services.
